chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The death from which you flee, it will surely meet you, up to His Words: 'that which you had done'.
He said: The years are numbered, then the months are numbered, then the days are numbered, then the hours are numbered, then the breaths are numbered.
So when their death comes, they would neither be delayed for a moment nor would they be quickened.
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam explain the precision of death in the Quranic verse 'Say: The death from which you flee will surely meet you'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine precision of death by detailing the meticulous counting of time units—from years down to individual breaths—highlighting that the appointed term (ajal) is fixed and immutable. This narration underscores the Shia theological concept of God's absolute control over the timing of the soul's departure, reassuring believers that death is not a random event but a calculated decree that neither advances nor delays. It serves as a reminder to reflect on the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of the Hereafter.
